encounters.title: Brothers of Destiny
encounters.story: Two brothers found Rumie together, then clash over whether trade or conquest will define the city.
encounters.beforeBattle: Before Rumie was an empire, it was an argument between two brothers.
encounters.afterBattle: Rolmus wins the first battle for Rumie's soul, but Remex's warning does not die.
dialogue: Narrator: Before Rumie was an empire, it was an argument between two brothers.
Rolmus: Trade builds cities. Trust builds roads.
Remex: Roads invite armies unless walls come first.
Rolmus: Then let Rumie be more than fear.
Remex: Or let it survive long enough to become anything at all.
endDialogue: Narrator: Rolmus wins the first battle for Rumie's soul, but Remex's warning does not die.
Rolmus: The first stones will be markets, not barracks.
Remex: And when raiders come?
Rolmus: Then we will defend what we built.
Remex: No, brother. One day you will build because you learned to defend.

bossAbility.title: Fortified Claim
bossAbility.text: The boss's first scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Remex: Fortified Claim

encounters.title: The Republic
encounters.story: Generations pass. Rumie grows wealthy, but corrupt senators, banks, runes, and legions begin shaping a fragile republic.
encounters.beforeBattle: Generations later, Rumie calls itself a republic, but gold has begun to vote louder than citizens.
encounters.afterBattle: The Republic survives, but its sickness has been named aloud.
dialogue: Narrator: Generations later, Rumie calls itself a republic, but gold has begun to vote louder than citizens.
Senator: The Republic endures because it is slow.
Tribune Marcell: Slow things are easy to buy.
Young Kaiser: Then someone must become too expensive to own.
Senator: Careful, boy. Men who speak that way become useful or dangerous.
endDialogue: Narrator: The Republic survives, but its sickness has been named aloud.
Tribune Marcell: You think exposing rot makes you clean?
Young Kaiser: No. It means the people can smell it too.
Senator: You have made enemies today.
Young Kaiser: Good. Then I know where to begin.

bossAbility.title: Fortified Claim
bossAbility.text: The boss's first scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Tribune Marcell: Fortified Claim

encounters.title: The Jewel
encounters.story: Kaiser rises as a beloved officer who walks among workers, pays debts, and exposes a governor protected by the aristocracy.
encounters.beforeBattle: Kaiser rises as a soldier of the people, paying debts the Senate pretends not to see.
encounters.afterBattle: Severan falls, and Kaiser becomes the Jewel of Rumie.
dialogue: Narrator: Kaiser rises as a soldier of the people, paying debts the Senate pretends not to see.
Severan: You mistake popularity for authority.
Kaiser: No. I mistake theft for treason.
Severan: The people cheer anyone who promises them bread.
Kaiser: Then perhaps you should have fed them.
endDialogue: Narrator: Severan falls, and Kaiser becomes the Jewel of Rumie.
Crowd: Kaiser! Kaiser! Kaiser!
Severan: They will love you until you ask something of them.
Kaiser: Then I will ask only what Rumie needs.
Severan: That is how every tyrant introduces himself.

bossAbility.title: Fortified Claim
bossAbility.text: The boss's first scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Corrupt Governor Severan: Fortified Claim

encounters.title: The Gaulic Wars
encounters.story: Northern tribes unite against Rumie. Kaiser turns frontier war into fame, wealth, and open trade routes.
encounters.beforeBattle: The northern frontier burns, and Kaiser marches toward the war that will make his name too large for the Senate.
encounters.afterBattle: The frontier opens, and Kaiser returns with veterans, wealth, and a legend the Senate cannot easily command.
dialogue: Narrator: The northern frontier burns, and Kaiser marches toward the war that will make his name too large for the Senate.
Vercan: Your roads end here, jewel prince.
Kaiser: Roads do not end. They arrive.
Vercan: Then arrive with steel.
Kaiser: I brought more than steel. I brought Rumie.
endDialogue: Narrator: The frontier opens, and Kaiser returns with veterans, wealth, and a legend the Senate cannot easily command.
Vercan: You win land. You do not win memory.
Kaiser: Memory follows roads too.
Vercan: Then one day your empire will remember every place it wounded.
Kaiser: And every place it raised from ruin.

bossAbility.title: Fortified Claim
bossAbility.text: The boss's first scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Gaulic Warchief Vercan: Fortified Claim

encounters.title: The Three Runes
encounters.story: Kaiser discovers vaults of Strength, Protection, and Experience, then begins binding sacred runes to the legions.
encounters.beforeBattle: Beneath conquered lands, Kaiser finds vaults older than Rumie itself.
encounters.afterBattle: The runes answer Kaiser, and Rumie's legions become more than soldiers.
dialogue: Narrator: Beneath conquered lands, Kaiser finds vaults older than Rumie itself.
Guardian: Strength without wisdom breaks itself.
Kaiser: Then I will take wisdom too.
Guardian: All conquerors say that before the vault closes.
Kaiser: I am not here to conquer the runes. I am here to make Rumie worthy of them.
endDialogue: Narrator: The runes answer Kaiser, and Rumie's legions become more than soldiers.
Guardian: You have taken Strength. You have taken Protection. You have taken Experience.
Kaiser: Then Rumie will endure.
Guardian: No. Rumie will become harder to kill.
Kaiser: For an empire, that may be the same thing.

bossAbility.title: Senate Pressure
bossAbility.text: The boss's final scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Ancient Rune Guardian: Senate Pressure

encounters.title: The First Empire Bank
encounters.story: Kaiser returns to build roads, grain systems, public works, and banking reforms while saboteurs try to break Rumie's markets.
encounters.beforeBattle: Kaiser turns from conquest to reform, but money resists command as fiercely as armies do.
encounters.afterBattle: The markets hold, and the people begin trusting Kaiser more than the Republic itself.
dialogue: Narrator: Kaiser turns from conquest to reform, but money resists command as fiercely as armies do.
Merchant: The city eats because credit moves.
Brutus: And if one man commands the credit?
Kaiser: Then one man answers if the people starve.
Brutus: Or one man decides who deserves bread.
endDialogue: Narrator: The markets hold, and the people begin trusting Kaiser more than the Republic itself.
Merchant: The grain arrives. The banks open. The streets are calm.
Brutus: Calm is not the same as free.
Kaiser: Hunger is not freedom either.
Brutus: No. But a fed people may still wake in chains.

bossAbility.title: Senate Pressure
bossAbility.text: The boss's final scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Market Collapse: Senate Pressure

encounters.title: The Crossing
encounters.story: The Senate orders Kaiser to surrender command. Brutus pleads for restraint, but Kaiser marches and civil war begins.
encounters.beforeBattle: The Senate orders Kaiser to surrender command. Between law and loyalty, Rumie holds its breath.
encounters.afterBattle: Kaiser crosses the line, and the Republic becomes a battlefield.
dialogue: Narrator: The Senate orders Kaiser to surrender command. Between law and loyalty, Rumie holds its breath.
Brutus: Kaiser, do not do this.
Kaiser: If I surrender, Rumie returns to corruption.
Brutus: Then save the Republic.
Kaiser: I intend to.
Brutus: You cannot save a thing by standing above it.
endDialogue: Narrator: Kaiser crosses the line, and the Republic becomes a battlefield.
Cassius: You have declared war on Rumie.
Kaiser: I have declared war on the men who sold it.
Brutus: You crossed with soldiers, not arguments.
Kaiser: Arguments failed the hungry. Soldiers will not.

bossAbility.title: Senate Pressure
bossAbility.text: The boss's final scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Senate General Cassius: Senate Pressure

encounters.title: The Last Republic
encounters.story: Rumie burns as legions and senators collide. Kaiser wins the city, but Brutus survives the fall of the old order.
encounters.beforeBattle: The old order makes its final stand, and Brutus faces the man he once hoped would save it.
encounters.afterBattle: The Republic still speaks, but it no longer rules.
dialogue: Narrator: The old order makes its final stand, and Brutus faces the man he once hoped would save it.
Brutus: You have saved Rumie by conquering it.
Kaiser: I have saved Rumie from men who sold it.
Brutus: Then we are both traitors.
Kaiser: Perhaps. But only one of us is still useful.
endDialogue: Narrator: The Republic still speaks, but it no longer rules.
Brutus: Listen to the silence after victory.
Kaiser: I hear rebuilding.
Brutus: I hear fear learning to applaud.
Kaiser: Then teach it courage, Brutus. Do not ask me to restore cowardice.

bossAbility.title: Senate Pressure
bossAbility.text: The boss's final scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Brutus: Senate Pressure

encounters.title: Emperor of Gold
encounters.story: At Kaiser's peak, roads, banks, and legions flourish, but prisoners, taxes, and central rule make citizens question the jewel.
encounters.beforeBattle: Rumie prospers beneath Kaiser, but gold can gild a cage as easily as a crown.
encounters.afterBattle: Kaiser reaches the height of power, and Rumie begins to wonder whether rescue has become rule.
dialogue: Narrator: Rumie prospers beneath Kaiser, but gold can gild a cage as easily as a crown.
Senator: Prosperity is not freedom.
Kaiser: Freedom without bread is a slogan.
Brutus: And bread without law is obedience.
Kaiser: Law failed when it served only those who could purchase it.
endDialogue: Narrator: Kaiser reaches the height of power, and Rumie begins to wonder whether rescue has become rule.
Senator: The roads are full. The banks are strong. The prisons are fuller.
Kaiser: Order has a cost.
Brutus: You once called that cost theft.
Kaiser: I was younger then.
Brutus: No. You were clearer.

bossAbility.title: Imperial Doctrine
bossAbility.text: The boss's final scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Rebel Senate Coalition: Imperial Doctrine

encounters.title: The Ides of Rumie
encounters.story: Kaiser stabilizes the empire, yet the conspiracy reaches the Senate floor. This chapter frames the tragedy more than the victory.
encounters.beforeBattle: The conspiracy reaches the Senate floor, where gratitude, fear, and betrayal wear the same robes.
encounters.afterBattle: Kaiser falls, but the empire does not. His killers destroy the man and preserve the myth.
dialogue: Narrator: The conspiracy reaches the Senate floor, where gratitude, fear, and betrayal wear the same robes.
Kaiser: You too, Brutus?
Brutus: I do this for Rumie.
Kaiser: No. You do it because Rumie no longer needs you.
Brutus: I do it because Rumie should need no one man.
endDialogue: Narrator: Kaiser falls, but the empire does not. His killers destroy the man and preserve the myth.
Brutus: It is done.
Conspirator: Then why are they not cheering?
Brutus: Because they loved him.
Conspirator: And now?
Brutus: Now they will remember him better than he was.

bossAbility.title: Imperial Doctrine
bossAbility.text: The boss's last two scripted attacks each turn get +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Brutus and the Conspirators: Imperial Doctrine

encounters.title: War of the Successors
encounters.story: After Kaiser dies, Bobei seeks vengeance while Brutus tries to restore the Republic from the ruins.
encounters.beforeBattle: Kaiser's death leaves Rumie with grief, ambition, and armies looking for a name to follow.
encounters.afterBattle: Brutus loses the future, and the Republic becomes a memory carried by the empire that replaces it.
dialogue: Narrator: Kaiser's death leaves Rumie with grief, ambition, and armies looking for a name to follow.
Bobei: You killed a man and woke an empire.
Brutus: I killed a tyrant.
Bobei: Then why does Rumie weep?
Brutus: Because grief is easier than liberty.
endDialogue: Narrator: Brutus loses the future, and the Republic becomes a memory carried by the empire that replaces it.
Brutus: I wanted Rumie to stand without a master.
Bobei: You left it leaderless in a storm.
Brutus: And you would give it another master?
Bobei: I would give it an heir.
Brutus: Then Kaiser wins, even dead.

bossAbility.title: Imperial Doctrine
bossAbility.text: The boss's last two scripted attacks each turn get +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Brutus: Imperial Doctrine

encounters.title: The First Emperor
encounters.story: Augustus defeats Bobei, keeps the bank, legions, and rune program, restores Senate traditions, and leaves Rumie with an empire wearing republican robes.
encounters.beforeBattle: Augustus and Bobei clash over Kaiser's legacy: vengeance or settlement, sword or law.
encounters.afterBattle: Augustus wins. The Senate returns in ceremony, the empire remains in fact, and Rumie learns to call obedience tradition.
dialogue: Narrator: Augustus and Bobei clash over Kaiser's legacy: vengeance or settlement, sword or law.
Bobei: I was Kaiser's sword.
Augustus: And I will be his law.
Bobei: Law without fire is parchment.
Augustus: Fire without law is only smoke.
Old Senator: Perhaps the better question is whether Rumie could have survived without him.
endDialogue: Narrator: Augustus wins. The Senate returns in ceremony, the empire remains in fact, and Rumie learns to call obedience tradition.
Bobei: You kept the Senate's masks.
Augustus: People fear naked power.
Old Senator: And what should we call this new arrangement?
Augustus: Peace.
Bobei: Empire.
Augustus: In Rumie, they will learn to mean the same thing.

bossAbility.title: Imperial Doctrine
bossAbility.text: The boss's last two scripted attacks each turn get +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Bobei the Great: Imperial Doctrine

encounters.title: The Iron Roots
encounters.story: The Obsidian Lords drain the forests through Iron Root outposts while Leafen Gao begins a rebellion among starving villages.
encounters.beforeBattle: The Obsidian Lords drain the forest through Iron Root outposts, turning living land into tribute. Leafen Gao's rebellion begins among starving villages with little more than anger and patience.
encounters.afterBattle: The first chains break. The Sheen learn that roots can strangle as well as nourish.
dialogue: Narrator: Before Beli had a crown, the Obsidian Lords taught the forest to starve.
Leafen Gao: A root that drinks everything is not a root. It is a chain.
Blackthorn: Chains hold kingdoms together.
Leafen Gao: Then the forest will break yours.
Blackthorn: Break a chain, rebel, and you will learn how much it was holding back.
endDialogue: Narrator: The first Iron Root falls, and the villages remember that hunger can become courage.
Leafen Gao: Take the grain. Share it before nightfall.
Blackthorn: You have fed one valley and doomed ten more.
Leafen Gao: No. I have shown ten valleys where to begin.
Blackthorn: Then I will teach them what rebellion costs.

bossAbility.title: Ironroot Pressure
bossAbility.text: Odd-numbered boss attacks get +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Emperor Blackthorn: Ironroot Pressure

encounters.title: The Verdant Uprising
encounters.story: Hushan joins Leafen as the rebellion spreads against Ironbark, Thornclaw, and Rootlash.
encounters.beforeBattle: Hushan joins Leafen as the rebellion spreads through villages, groves, and hidden paths. The Thorn Guard believes a scattered forest cannot become an army.
encounters.afterBattle: The rebellion becomes a people. What began as hunger has grown into a shared memory of injustice.
dialogue: Narrator: Word of Leafen's victory moves faster than soldiers, and Hushan brings disciplined roots to wild hope.
Hushan: They say this rebellion is doomed.
Leafen Gao: Seeds are buried before they rise.
Ironbark: Then we will salt the soil.
Hushan: Salt washes away. Roots remember water.
endDialogue: Narrator: Thorn Guard banners fall in three valleys, and the uprising becomes a map.
Ironbark: You cannot command forests with songs.
Leafen Gao: No. But songs tell forests when to move.
Hushan: We do not need every tree to fight. Only enough to make the tyrant afraid of shade.
Ironbark: Then shade will burn.

bossAbility.title: Ironroot Pressure
bossAbility.text: Odd-numbered boss attacks get +1 value.
bossAbility.name: The Thorn Guard Commanders: Ironroot Pressure

encounters.title: Fall of the Obsidian Throne
encounters.story: Leshan and Dowan collapse the Iron Roots themselves, forcing Blackthorn into one last monstrous stand.
encounters.beforeBattle: Leshan and Dowan strike at the Iron Roots themselves, forcing Blackthorn into a final stand. If the root survives, the forest will never be free.
encounters.afterBattle: Blackthorn falls. The Sheen win their forest, but victory leaves them with the harder task of building a kingdom that does not become another chain.
dialogue: Narrator: Leshan and Dowan find the hidden roots beneath Blackthorn's throne, where every stolen harvest has been counted.
Leshan: Strike the root, not the branch.
Blackthorn: I am the root.
Leafen Gao: Then fall with it.
Blackthorn: Without me, the forest will devour itself.
endDialogue: Narrator: Blackthorn falls, and the Obsidian Throne cracks like winter bark.
Leafen Gao: No lord will drink the forest dry again.
Leshan: Then we must become more than rebels.
Hushan: Rebellion cuts. A kingdom must heal.
Leafen Gao: Then we begin with living soil, not stone.

bossAbility.title: Ironroot Pressure
bossAbility.text: Odd-numbered boss attacks get +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Blackthorn, Lord of Iron: Ironroot Pressure

encounters.title: Beli, Living City
encounters.story: The Sheen rebuild, found Beli, and begin the Root Network while a natural blight threatens the new kingdom.
encounters.beforeBattle: The Sheen found Beli and begin the Root Network, but nature itself tests the newborn kingdom through blight and scarcity. Rebellion must become stewardship.
encounters.afterBattle: Beli survives. The Sheen discover that a city can grow like a forest if its people accept patience as power.
dialogue: Narrator: The Sheen found Beli as a city grown from oath, root, and shelter.
Leafen Gao: We won a forest. Now we must make it a home.
Reane: Homes are grown, not declared.
The Great Blight: All growth returns to hunger.
Leafen Gao: Then hunger will find us planted together.
endDialogue: Narrator: Beli survives its first sickness, and the city learns that care can be a defense.
Reane: The blight did not vanish. It retreated.
Leafen Gao: Then we watch the soil.
The Great Blight: Watch. Worry. Wither. I am patient.
Reane: So are forests.

bossAbility.title: Ironroot Pressure
bossAbility.text: Odd-numbered boss attacks get +1 value.
bossAbility.name: The Great Blight: Ironroot Pressure

encounters.title: The Root Network
encounters.story: Dowan expands Sheen botanical science with barriers, shields, greenhouses, and trade routes, but the Ash Serpent burns the nodes.
encounters.beforeBattle: Dowan expands botanical science into roads, shields, greenhouses, and trade routes. The Ash Serpent burns the nodes, proving that connection also creates vulnerability.
encounters.afterBattle: The network bends instead of breaking. The Sheen learn that defense is not a wall, but a living system.
dialogue: Narrator: Dowan begins the Root Network, binding distant shelters through living paths beneath the earth.
Dowan: The network must bend before it spreads.
Bark Xin: And if fire follows the roots?
Dowan: Then we teach roots to carry rain.
Ash Serpent: Rain becomes steam. Roots become smoke.
endDialogue: Narrator: The first firebreak blooms, and the Root Network learns to survive attack.
Bark Xin: The burned nodes are already budding.
Dowan: A network is not one root. That is why it lives.
Ash Serpent: I will find the heart.
Dowan: You misunderstand us. We are learning not to have one.

bossAbility.title: Thorned Advance
bossAbility.text: The boss's first scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: The Ash Serpent: Thorned Advance

encounters.title: The Blooming Age
encounters.story: The Sheen enter a golden age of shelters, retreats, springs, and living greenhouses as a desert warlord tests the border.
encounters.beforeBattle: Shelters, retreats, springs, and greenhouses bring abundance, but prosperity attracts enemies from dry borders. The Drought King comes to prove growth can be starved.
encounters.afterBattle: The Blooming Age endures. The Sheen understand prosperity as preparation, not comfort.
dialogue: Narrator: Beli enters its blooming age, and prosperity spreads through shelters, springs, and greenhouses.
Reane: Prosperity is not how much we store. It is how much survives winter.
Drought King: I bring a longer winter.
Hushan: Then we bring deeper roots.
Drought King: Roots crack when the world forgets rain.
endDialogue: Narrator: The Drought King's army breaks at the living springs, and Beli's borders flower instead of harden.
Reane: Water belongs to need, not conquest.
Hushan: The border villages will have reservoirs by autumn.
Drought King: Mercy makes soft kingdoms.
Reane: Mercy made this one hard to kill.

bossAbility.title: Thorned Advance
bossAbility.text: The boss's first scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: The Drought King: Thorned Advance

encounters.title: The Court of Blossoms
encounters.story: Political factions emerge in Beli as Den tries to preserve stability while Aime and Tang rise through the court.
encounters.beforeBattle: As Beli blooms, politics rot quietly inside the court. Den watches nobles and ministers turn harmony into influence.
encounters.afterBattle: Den preserves stability for now. But the court has revealed a dangerous truth: a peaceful kingdom can still decay.
dialogue: Narrator: In peace, Beli grows a court, and every blossom learns the shadow of ambition.
Den: A court can rot while every garden blooms.
Hollowvine: Rot feeds the next garden.
Den: Not while I still prune.
Hollowvine: Prune too much and you become the knife, not the gardener.
endDialogue: Narrator: Hollowvine is exposed, but the Court of Blossoms has learned how quietly poison travels.
Den: Remove his seal. Leave his records.
Hollowvine: You will read them and find half the court inside.
Den: Then half the court will answer.
Hollowvine: Careful, Den. Roots tangle below every throne.

bossAbility.title: Thorned Advance
bossAbility.text: The boss's first scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Minister Hollowvine: Thorned Advance

encounters.title: The Reformer
encounters.story: Tang sees inequality and stagnation, introduces reforms that truly help, and wins sympathy against corrupt nobles.
encounters.beforeBattle: Tang rises against inequality and noble stagnation, promising reforms that return life to the poor. His cause is just, but justice can grow thorns.
encounters.afterBattle: Tang wins the people's faith. Reform becomes power, and power begins asking for obedience.
dialogue: Narrator: Tang rises from the court with reform in his hands and anger beneath his patience.
Tang: Tradition has become a fence around empty soil.
Goldroot: Empty soil is still mine.
Tang: Not after the roots remember the poor.
Goldroot: The poor need shade, not power.
endDialogue: Narrator: Goldroot's estates open, and Tang becomes the voice of those Beli forgot.
Tang: Every storehouse will answer to the hunger around it.
Goldroot: You call seizure justice because applause makes it warm.
Tang: I call it justice because children will eat tonight.
Goldroot: Tonight is not a constitution.

bossAbility.title: Thorned Advance
bossAbility.text: The boss's first scripted attack each turn gets +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Lord Goldroot: Thorned Advance

encounters.title: Thorned Crown
encounters.story: Tang centralizes power and creates the Thornblades, while Ringan, a former ally, tries to stop his imbalance.
encounters.beforeBattle: Tang creates the Thornblades and centralizes authority to protect reform from corruption. Ringan sees the danger: a cure becoming a crown.
encounters.afterBattle: Tang defeats his critics, but the kingdom is no longer merely healing. It is being commanded.
dialogue: Narrator: Tang's reforms harden into command, and the Thornblades rise where councils once argued.
Ringan: You wanted reform. This is control.
Tang: Control is reform that cannot be bribed.
Ringan: And cannot be questioned.
Tang: Questions are how the hungry are delayed.
endDialogue: Narrator: Ringan retreats, and Tang takes the thorned crown no one officially offered.
Ringan: You are protecting the people from their own voices.
Tang: I am protecting them from the voices that purchase them.
Ringan: You have made distrust into law.
Tang: I have made weakness answerable.

bossAbility.title: Living Siege
bossAbility.text: Odd-numbered boss attacks get +1 value.
bossAbility.name: Ringan: Living Siege

encounters.title: The War of Roots
encounters.story: Civil war burns the forests as shelters are weaponized and the Root Network collapses under Ashroot, Briarfang, and Ironvine.
encounters.beforeBattle: Civil war spreads through the forest. Shelters become forts, roads carry armies, and the Root Network becomes a battlefield.
encounters.afterBattle: The old harmony burns. The Sheen learn that even living systems can be weaponized when fear takes root.
dialogue: Narrator: Civil war reaches the Root Network, and the roads built for bread begin carrying blades.
Dowan: I built these roads to feed cities.
Ashroot: Roads also carry armies.
Hushan: Then we cut the roads and save the roots.
Briarfang: Cut them, and the cities starve for your conscience.
endDialogue: Narrator: The Thornblade generals fall, but every victory severs another living path.
Dowan: We saved the nodes by burning the bridges between them.
Hushan: Better wounded roots than captured ones.
Ringan: Do not comfort yourselves. We are pruning a kingdom with fire.
Dowan: Then we remember every branch we took.

bossAbility.title: Living Siege
bossAbility.text: Odd-numbered boss attacks get +1 value, and the boss restores 1 life at the start of each turn.
bossAbility.name: The Thornblade Generals: Living Siege

encounters.title: Fall of Thorn Mang
encounters.story: Tang realizes too late what his reforms became, then falls as healer, commander, and living thorn avatar.
encounters.beforeBattle: Tang stands as healer, reformer, ruler, and living thorn avatar. He finally sees the pain caused in the name of survival, but too late to step aside peacefully.
encounters.afterBattle: Tang falls. The Sheen mourn both the tyrant he became and the reformer he once was.
dialogue: Narrator: Tang waits at Thorn Mang, where reform, fear, and living thorn have become one body.
Tang: I only wanted the kingdom to live.
Reane: Then why does it bleed when you speak?
Tang: Because I mistook pain for pruning.
Dowan: Then let the wound close before the whole forest scars.
endDialogue: Narrator: Tang falls, and for a moment even the thorns seem relieved.
Tang: Was I wrong from the beginning?
Reane: No. That is why this hurts.
Dowan: Good roots can still strangle when they forget light.
Tang: Then teach them better than I did.

bossAbility.title: Living Siege
bossAbility.text: Odd-numbered boss attacks get +1 value, and the boss restores 1 life at the start of each turn.
bossAbility.name: Tang, Crown of Thorns: Living Siege

encounters.title: The Green Era
encounters.story: Dowan restores the Root Network, shelters, healing, greenhouses, and balance after the civil war.
encounters.beforeBattle: Dowan inherits a wounded kingdom. The Root Network must be restored, not as a tool of control, but as a promise of balance.
encounters.afterBattle: The Green Era begins. The Sheen choose renewal over revenge, and remember that growth without harmony becomes overgrowth.
dialogue: Narrator: After civil war, Dowan faces the hardest enemy left: rebuilding without repeating the wound.
Dowan: Growth without harmony becomes overgrowth.
Reane: Tradition without growth becomes ash.
Dowan: Then wisdom is knowing when to nurture and when to prune.
The Great Renewal: All new growth must decide what old roots deserve to remain.
endDialogue: Narrator: The Root Network blooms again, slower now, wiser for every scar beneath it.
Dowan: No single root will rule the forest.
Reane: And no old branch will be kept only because it is old.
The Great Renewal: Then Beli is not restored. It is changed.
Dowan: That is how living things endure.

bossAbility.title: Living Siege
bossAbility.text: Odd-numbered boss attacks get +1 value, and the boss restores 1 life at the start of each turn.
bossAbility.name: The Great Renewal: Living Siege

encounters.title: The Tax of the Tides
encounters.story: King Ludvik's tribute fleets bleed Ristus while royal collectors seize treasure from every captain and family.
encounters.beforeBattle: King Ludvik's tribute fleets bleed Ristus dry while royal collectors seize treasure from captains and families. Lafayette sees a kingdom drowning in its own greed.
encounters.afterBattle: The tax fleet is broken. The Frumo learn that the sea does not belong only to crowns.
dialogue: Narrator: Before revolution had a flag, it had a ledger soaked in seawater.
Tax Collector: By order of King Ludvik, every hold, net, vault, and table owes tribute.
Lafayette: The sea gives enough for all Frumo. Your king has taught it to starve.
Tax Collector: Then all Frumo can pay the king, and thank him for permission to sail.
Lafayette: The tide is turning against your vaults.

encounters.afterBattle: The voices become a movement. The monarchy still stands, but the Frumo have learned to imagine life without it.

Danton: Then Coral Bay will learn a new language.
Lafayette: Let that language be freedom, not merely revenge.

Mirabeau: They heard us.
Marat: Hearing is not enough. Fear must change sides.
Lafayette: Careful. If fear leads us, we inherit Ludvik's throne in another shape.

encounters.afterBattle: Silver Shoals falls. The revolution proves that courage, tide, and timing can defeat inherited power.

Carnot: Courage is loud until cannon fire teaches it discipline.

Danton: Walls are where frightened kingdoms hide their truth.
Marat: Open the vaults. Let the people see what hunger purchased.

Lafayette: No. But I know how easy you made suffering look.
endDialogue: Narrator: The palace gates open from the inside, because even royal guards have families beneath the tide.

Lafayette: You mistook carrying for owning.

encounters.title: The Trial of the King

encounters.beforeBattle: The Frumo must decide whether Ludvik should be spared, imprisoned, or executed. Justice and vengeance begin wearing the same face.
encounters.afterBattle: The king's fate divides the revolution. Freedom has won its first victory and immediately faces its first moral wound.
dialogue: Narrator: With Ludvik chained, the revolution faces a question no victory can answer cleanly.

Lafayette: Justice is not hunger with a blade.

Robespier: Mercy is how tyrants learn to swim back.
endDialogue: Narrator: The verdict divides the republic before it has even learned to stand.
Lafayette: We have made the crown mortal. That should have been enough.
Robespier: Enough is the word cautious men use when courage becomes expensive.

encounters.afterBattle: The terror consumes itself. The Frumo learn that a revolution can drown in the name of purity.
dialogue: Narrator: Victory curdles into suspicion, and the revolution begins searching its own reflection for enemies.
Robespier: The enemies of freedom wear many faces.
Marat: Then you will soon accuse the mirror.
Robespier: Mercy is the weapon of tyrants.
Marat: And purity is the mask fear wears when it wants a judge's chair.

Marat: You scrubbed it until it bled.

encounters.beforeBattle: Coalition fleets gather while the republic trembles. Polea wins impossible battles and gives the Frumo a hero when they most need one.
encounters.afterBattle: Polea saves the republic. In doing so, he becomes the one person the republic fears it cannot survive without.

Admiral: Tomorrow it will need permission.

encounters.beforeBattle: The Council grants Polea more command with every crisis. Each emergency passes, but his authority remains.
encounters.afterBattle: The Council yields piece by piece. Polea has not seized the republic all at once; he has taught it to depend on him.
dialogue: Narrator: Each emergency passes, but the authority granted to survive it remains in Polea's hands.
Councilor: You were given command for one crisis.
Polea: The crisis learned to change names.
Councilor: So did ambition.
Polea: Ambition built the fleet you now hide behind.
endDialogue: Narrator: The Council yields a little more power and tells itself survival is not surrender.
Councilor: You have made obedience feel practical.
Polea: I have made disorder answerable.

encounters.title: The Frumo Empire
encounters.story: Polea crowns himself Lord Commander of All Frumo: no king, no council, no election, only command.
encounters.beforeBattle: Polea crowns himself Lord Commander of All Frumo. He claims unity, order, and survival; his shadow whispers another word: ambition.
encounters.afterBattle: The republic becomes an empire. The Frumo are strong, victorious, and no longer free in the way they once demanded.
dialogue: Narrator: Polea crowns himself without calling it a crown, and the republic learns how command can dress as necessity.
Polea: I freed the Frumo from kings.
Shadow: And gave them a commander instead.
Polea: Better one helm than a thousand drowning hands.
Shadow: Say it plainly. You trust the people only after they obey.
endDialogue: Narrator: The banners change, the fleets expand, and citizens argue whether empire is betrayal or the price of order.
Polea: I have united what councils nearly drowned.
Shadow: You have mistaken still water for peace.

encounters.title: The Hundred Fleets
encounters.story: Polea's armadas dominate Reath's oceans as rival Frumo sea powers unite against his endless victories.
encounters.beforeBattle: Rival sea powers unite against Polea's endless victories. The oceans themselves seem to ask whether one commander can own every tide.
encounters.afterBattle: Polea dominates the seas. But each victory makes his empire wider, colder, and harder to hold.
dialogue: Narrator: Rival sea powers unite, not because they agree with each other, but because Polea has taught them what fear shares.
Coral Envoy: The seas do not belong to one captain.
Polea: Then why do they answer mine?
Brasswater Admiral: Because fear sounds like obedience.
Polea: Fear is only the first lesson. Order is the second.
endDialogue: Narrator: The hundred fleets scatter, and Polea's map grows wider than any Frumo ruler has held.
Coral Envoy: You win waters faster than you can know them.
Polea: I do not need to know every wave to command the tide.

encounters.title: The Frozen Sea
encounters.story: Polea attempts to conquer the northern oceans, but storms, ice, hunger, and a leviathan shatter the once-invincible navy.
encounters.beforeBattle: Polea sails north to conquer what no fleet has held. Ice, hunger, storms, and silence await the navy that believed itself invincible.
encounters.afterBattle: The fleet shatters. Polea survives, but his myth is cracked by a sea that refuses command.
dialogue: Narrator: Polea sails north to conquer the only ocean that has never learned his name.
Polea: No tide has ever refused me.
Ice Leviathan: This is not tide. This is silence.
Polea: Then I will break silence too.
Ice Leviathan: Command freezes before it reaches me.
endDialogue: Narrator: The northern fleet shatters, and for the first time Polea returns with fewer ships than excuses.
Polea: Storms are accidents. Ice is weather. Hunger is logistics.
Ice Leviathan: Name your defeat smaller if it comforts you.

encounters.beforeBattle: Former allies and rival fleets gather for one final reckoning. Polea insists history will understand him; Lafayette insists the living cannot wait for history.
encounters.afterBattle: Polea falls. The Council is restored, but the Frumo remember how easily freedom can become command when fear asks for a hero.
dialogue: Narrator: Former allies gather with rival fleets, and the last battle asks whether Frumo can survive its greatest hero.
Polea: I freed the Frumo. I united them. I made them strong.
Lafayette: And then you made them yours.
Polea: If that makes me a tyrant, history may judge me.
Councilor: The living will judge first.
endDialogue: Narrator: Polea falls, but no one celebrates for long. The republic has learned what fear can build from gratitude.
Lafayette: Restore the Council. Restore the arguments. Restore the burden of choice.

characters.name: Sheen Narrator
characters.description: A calm, reflective voice that treats the Sheen story like a forest history told after many generations. The narrator should feel wise rather than dramatic, carrying both wonder and grief as the campaign moves from rebellion to renewal.

characters.name: Leafen Gao
characters.description: Leafen Gao begins as a gentle revolutionary who refuses to let hunger become normal. He is patient, soft-spoken, and deeply rooted in compassion, but his calm hides extraordinary resolve. In the early campaign he gives the Sheen their moral center: resistance is justified only if it grows into shelter, food, and a livable kingdom.

characters.name: Emperor Blackthorn
characters.description: Blackthorn is the ruler of the Obsidian Lords, an imperial figure who believes extraction, fear, and hierarchy are the only forces strong enough to keep the forest from chaos. He should feel cold, old, and immovable, like iron grown through living roots. He is not frantic; he is certain.

characters.name: Hushan
characters.description: Hushan gives Leafen's uprising structure. Where Leafen inspires, Hushan organizes, protects, and makes hard battlefield decisions. He should sound grounded and dependable, with a soldier's economy of words and a guardian's concern for the villages under his care.

characters.name: Ironbark
characters.description: Ironbark represents Blackthorn's military order: blunt, punitive, and contemptuous of rebellion. He is less philosophical than Blackthorn and more immediately threatening, the kind of commander who believes burning one valley can keep ten obedient.

characters.name: Leshan
characters.description: Leshan is a quiet tactical mind who sees systems beneath symbols. She understands that defeating Blackthorn requires attacking the hidden machinery of power, not merely winning battles. Her voice should be precise, restrained, and quietly brave.

characters.name: Reane
characters.description: Reane embodies Sheen care at its most mature. She is a healer, builder, and moral critic who understands that homes, laws, and traditions must be grown with attention. Her warmth should never sound weak; she is often the character who sees the wound before the warriors do.

characters.name: The Great Blight
characters.description: The Great Blight is less a villain than a living pressure: disease, scarcity, and decay given voice. It should sound slow, patient, and unsettling, as if it has watched forests rise and rot many times before. It opposes the Sheen by making survival itself uncertain.

characters.name: Dowan
characters.description: Dowan is an engineer-scientist of living systems, responsible for turning Sheen ideals into infrastructure. He is curious, careful, and humane, but the civil war forces him to face how any network can be captured or weaponized. His voice should be thoughtful, analytical, and quietly burdened.

characters.name: Bark Xin
characters.description: Bark Xin is a field guardian who tests Dowan's ideas against danger. He is cautious without being cowardly, practical without being cynical, and often asks the question that keeps invention from becoming fantasy.

characters.name: The Ash Serpent
characters.description: The Ash Serpent is wildfire with intent. It should feel dry, hissing, and predatory, a force that mocks the Sheen belief that every system can bend and survive. Its purpose is to test whether the Root Network is truly resilient.

characters.name: The Drought King
characters.description: The Drought King is a severe ruler shaped by barren lands. He sees mercy as softness and abundance as something to seize before it disappears. His voice should be proud, harsh, and sun-baked, but not foolish; he is what survival looks like without compassion.

characters.name: Den
characters.description: Den is a courtly stabilizer who understands that peace creates its own dangers. He is diplomatic, suspicious, and careful with power. He should sound controlled and observant, like someone pruning corruption before it becomes visible from the road.

characters.name: Minister Hollowvine
characters.description: Hollowvine is rot with manners. He believes corruption is not a failure of politics but one of its natural nutrients. His voice should be smooth, patient, and poisonous, the kind of person who makes decay sound practical.

characters.name: Tang
characters.description: Tang begins with real compassion for the poor and real anger at stagnant elites. His tragedy is that he increasingly treats opposition as sabotage and delay as cruelty. He should start earnest and wounded, then become sharper, more commanding, and more isolated as reform hardens into control.

characters.name: Lord Goldroot
characters.description: Goldroot is the voice of comfortable tradition. He does not think of himself as evil; he thinks order belongs to those who already own it. His voice should be entitled, polished, and dismissive, with flashes of fear when Tang proves popular.

characters.name: Ringan
characters.description: Ringan once believed in Tang's reforms, which makes his opposition personal and painful. He represents the line between justice and control. His voice should carry grief, frustration, and courage rather than simple hostility.

characters.name: Ashroot
characters.description: Ashroot is the military face of Tang's hardened reforms. He sees roads, shelters, and networks as strategic assets first and civic promises second. His voice should be severe and efficient.

characters.name: Briarfang
characters.description: Briarfang is a sharper, more mocking Thornblade commander who understands the moral leverage of necessity. He should sound like someone who knows cutting supply lines will hurt civilians and uses that fact as a weapon.

characters.name: The Great Renewal
characters.description: The Great Renewal is the sacred pressure of regrowth after catastrophe. It is not sentimental; it asks what deserves to remain and what must be transformed. The voice should feel ancient, green, and impersonal, like a forest speaking in seasons.

characters.name: Beli, Living City
characters.text: After your second block each turn, your next attack with cost 10+ gains +2 value.

characters.name: Lord Commander Polea
characters.text: Once per turn, choose 1: put a card from your hand into an empty lane you control; switch the lanes of up to 2 cards you control; look at 1 face-down card; or one card you control gets +1 value until end of turn.

announcements.selected: All sails answer the Lord Commander. Make ready.
announcements.clicked: The tide favors the captain who gives it orders.
announcements.wounded: Twenty-one life. Reef the sails and hold the line.
announcements.critical: Ten life. One last broadside decides the sea.
announcements.denied: A poor wager, captain.

characters.name: Lafayette
characters.text: Once per turn, you may swap a lane card with a card from your hand.

characters.name: Ristus, Sunken City
characters.text: Your first card played each turn with a consecutive value of the last card played gets +2.

characters.name: Focus, Conductor of Progress
characters.text: Whenever you overpay for a card by 2 or more, put an acceleration counter on this. Once per turn, you may remove an acceleration counter: target card gets +1 value until end of turn.

announcements.selected: Conductor online. Progress is now inevitable.
announcements.clicked: Every mechanism has a purpose. Including you.
announcements.wounded: Life reserve at twenty-one. Redirecting power to defense.
announcements.critical: Critical threshold: ten. Release every safeguard.
announcements.denied: Insufficient power allocation.

characters.name: Hera
characters.text: Once per turn: If you've played a card of a suit this turn, you may use a card of the same suit to pay 2 more than its value.

characters.name: Constanti, Technology Hub
characters.text: Each turn, your first two attacks after the first that have a different suit from your previous attack get +1 value.

characters.name: Broodmother Zalara
characters.text: At the start of your turn, create an Egg in an empty lane. Once per turn, hatch an Egg into a Worker, Soldier, or Guard.

announcements.selected: The brood awakens. One will become many.
announcements.clicked: Hatch. Adapt. Consume. Begin again.
announcements.wounded: Twenty-one life. The wounded brood evolves.
announcements.critical: Ten life. Break every shell. Release the swarm.
announcements.denied: The brood is not ready to strike.

characters.name: K'Lar, Biomass Keeper
characters.text: Once per turn, sacrifice two Underlings you control to draw one card.

characters.name: Brood Nest
characters.text: The first time you hatch each turn, you may hatch a second Egg into a Worker.

characters.name: High Marshal Alden
characters.text: Once per turn, deploy the top card of your deck to an empty lane if it is a Servitor with printed value 3 or less.

announcements.selected: Vanguard deployed. Every soldier to their mark.
announcements.clicked: Plan the descent. Control the ground. Finish the mission.
announcements.wounded: Twenty-one life. Tighten formation and hold the outpost.
announcements.critical: Ten life. All units, execute final deployment.
announcements.denied: Deployment parameters are incomplete.

characters.text: Once per turn, put a card from your hand on top of your deck. Your next payment this turn gets +2 value.

characters.name: Vanguard Outpost
characters.text: Whenever a Servitor enters one of your lanes directly from your deck, it gets +1 value until end of turn.
